messages.body_plain:
On Dec 25, 2012, at 5:20 AM, elad bensal <bens...@gmail.com> wrote:

> hi
>
> i want to use the function "ripple" with method="likelihood"
> i read the chapter about the hidden markov .i saw that in the backcross model
> the rqtl library assumes (page 373 in the book) PIE(AB)=PIE(AA)=1/2 i want to ask if i have PIE(AB)=PIE(AA)=p and p doesnt equal to 1/2 how does it affect the LOD in the way that the RQTL calculates it..?

I assume you mean Pr(AB) = p and Pr(AA) = 1-p for some p.

If there is reasonably complete genotype data, results won't be much affected by the presence of such segregation distortion.

> what is the connection between the formula for detection of genotyping error(page 380 in the book) to the LOD score that we calculate by ripple with the method "likelihood"
> the likelihood that i think it should be
> P1^(Kobs)*(1-P1)^(N-Kobs)/(P2^(Kobs)*(1-P2)^(N-Kobs))
> i belive that the RQTL makes this calculation with P2=1/2 am i wrong?

I don't understand what you are after, regarding the connection between the likelihood calculations in ripple() and the genotyping error LOD scores.

R/qtl does all calculations for a backcross assuming equal segregation of alleles, Pr(AA) = Pr(AB) = 1/2 in a backcross.

karl

messages.subject: Plots of rf LOD vs rf value
messages.subject_clean: Plots of rf LOD vs rf value
messages.body_plain:
Karl:

I am conducting genotypic error checking in the combined data of four populations; each has about 250 F2 individuals, and in each pop 22 high and 22 lo trait value individuals were selectively genotyped.  Thus, there are 44 x 4 = 176 genotyped individuals and there are 593 SNP markers segregating in the combined data set.

I generated a plot of rf LOD scores versus rf value for all possible marker pairs - see the attached PDF (which includes a zoom-in page).  Most of the outlier marker pairs arise from one (or two) problematic marker(s) that are repeat members of those pairs.  My 1st criterion for an outlier is rf>0.85, so I can easily identify the problem markers by examining the output of this command: print(rf85 <- which(rf[,1:totmar(OBJNAME)]>0.85, arr.in <http://arr.in>=TRUE))

However, for my second outlier criterion is a rf LOD score GT 4.0).  The problem here, of course, is that there are rf values LT 0.50 and GT 0.5, and I need a listing only of the latter.  Not being well-versed in R, I have tried for some time now to write some R code to do this listing but have failed so far.  To keep me from pulling the last hair  out of my head, would you be able to supply me with some R code to do this?  Many thanks if you can!

Jim

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] calc.errlod question (and R-coding help?)
messages.body_plain:
I would try to fix the map and the discrepancies between the genotype data and the genetic map, rather than omit markers with lots of indications of problems.

But, if you were to drop markers appearing multiple times in the output of top.errorlod(), you could use the table() function, something like the following:

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.errorlod(hyper)
top <- top.errorlod(hyper)
table(top[,3])
tab <- table(top[,3])
todrop <- names(tab[tab > 6])

karl

> Rqtl User Group & Karl:

> I have a question about dealing with the outputted results of the calc.errorlod cmd in my multiple F2 populations (n=~250) for which the two phenotypic decile extremes were selectively genotyped (SG) with 450 to 500 markers in a genome of 2300 cM Kosambi (i.e., about 1 marker on average per 5 cM of distance).
>
> The calc.errorlod cmd generates a large list of markers (see below example) in most of my F2 pops, primarily because the chromosome marker order and cM distances used in my *.csv file come from a published Ver. 4.0 (2010) marker map for soybean.  It has been acknowledged that this map (like all genetic maps) probably has some marker mis-order within tightly linked marker sets.  I surmise that such mis-order is probably reflected in the calc.errorlod cmd output as markers with repeated appearance (e.g.,  S30182, S14052).  I have too few genotyped individuals (50 in the decile SG’d 250 F2s) to construct a reliable intrinsic map for each F2, and the small F2 genotype numbers would likely have mis-order as well, not to mention unreliable marker distance estimates).  I will likely be some time before an updated Ver. 5.0 soybean genetic map is published.  In the meantime, I propose simply dropping  markers with multiple appearances in the below list (e.g., S30182, S14052), given that the removal of one tightly linked but mis-ordered marker would obviously still leave me with good markers in that close genomic region to use going forward.
>
> What do you Rqtl users think about my proposal?
>
> BTW, if I were to do this dropping of markers with n as the chosen number of repeat occurrences (e.g., say n = 4 or more), is there some simple R code I could use to put those markers into a todrop object?  The reason I ask for R help is that I would like to automate this process in a batchfile that I now use for error-checking in my multiple F2 populations.  Currently, I do it this kind of dropping manually and then use some code Karl provided to me earlier for “cleaning up” (i.e., change marker genotype to missing) the remaining markers in the below list (assumed – with some risk, of course- to be erroneous genotypings for a LOD score of 6 or more).

> Jim

messages.body_plain:

karl
--------

Subject: mqmscan vs mqmscanall
Date: January 10, 2013 8:20:32 PM CST

Hi,

I have been using R-QTL for a medical research project I am running and I have come across an error. I have successfully carried out single trait analyses using mqmscan, however when trying to perform multiple trait analyses I would like to assess several traits together using mqmscanall but not include sex as a phenotype in this analysis. It seems that when I get rid of the information about sex and reload the file the program "assumes all individuals are females" and then still includes sex as a phenotype in the multiple trait analysis. Is there any way to specify which phenotype columns to analyse in the mqmscanall. Alternatively is there anyway to stop the read.cross function from adding any information about sex?

Sorry I hope this is clear. I really appreciate any help I can get, thanks very much for your time.

Cheers

messages.subject: Re: mqmscan vs mqmscanall: sex phenotype
messages.body_plain:
If you have X chromosome genotypes, then sex will be needed in order to make use of it.

But mqmscanall currently only works with *all* of the phenotypes; you can't yet specify particular columns.

You could run the individual phenotypes of interest separately (perhaps within a for loop).
Or you could omit the X chromosome.

karl

messages.subject: LOD scores and map extension
messages.body_plain: I am doing QTL analysis with an introgression strain, meaning that all recombination breakpoints are clustered in particular areas of the chromosome. This results in considerable map extension, where markers from the introgressed region clump together and those in the native region clump together.  When plotting the results of scanone, this also results in an uptick in the LOD curve over the large gap areas. This doesn't occur in other programs like QTLCartographer (which has its own problems, I'd rather not use it). Is there a reason for this? Should I just try and get around it by imposing map distances on the markers?  It is mostly an aesthetic problem, getting the plots into a publishable condition is difficult when they look rather misleading.  Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How can I specify F1xF1 family as a covariate for an MQM model with a complicated cross design?
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] How can I specify F1xF1 family as a covariate for an MQM model with a complicated cross design?
messages.body_plain:
> I'm stumped as to how to specify family as a cofactor for an MQM model I'm trying to test.  I am working with a complex outbred mapping population in which 40 F1 fish (from an intercross between two species) were allowed to freely interbred in a pond, in order to produce F2 hybrids for mapping.

In the QTL formula, you need to refer to the columns in the covariate matrix by their names.  It would be best to give them simpler names than they currently have:

colnames(family_cofactor) <- paste("fam", 1:ncol(family_cofactor), sep="")

Then I'd use a bit of code to make the long formula, rather than typing it.

myformula <- "y ~ Q1+Q2+Q3+Q4+Q5+Q6+Q9+Q10+Q11+Q12+Q13+Q1:Q11+Q1:Q13+Q3:Q12+Q4:Q12+Q10:Q11"
myformula <- paste(myformula, "+", paste(colnames(family_cofactor), collapse="+"), sep="+")

output <- fitqtl(miAll.29fam.gp <http://miAll.29fam.gp>, pheno.col="isotope_pc1", covar=family_cofactor,
                 qtl=All_Candidate_QTL_for_PC1, get.ests=TRUE, method="hk",
                 formula=myformula)

karl

karl

On Jan 28, 2013, at 10:25 AM, HASmith <hasmith...@gmail.com> wrote:

The scale is relatively arbitrary.  We threshold the high LOD scores (argument zmax, with default value 10) and transform the recombination fractions to be on a similar scale (with the formula   -4*(log2(rf) + 1)/12 * zmax ).

> For me an even better result would be perhaps if it were possible to generate a plot showing all markers on the x-axis, and the recombination frequency on the y-axis. Yet as this is plotting against lod score, it's not quite what I need. The closest I came up with was to use write.csv to save the "rf" matrix to a file, then take the average down each column for a value of the recombination frequency at that marker. Does this sound correct, or is there a better way? Sorry if it's a somewhat basic question.

I'm not sure what you're trying to look at.  There is an estimated recombination fraction and LOD score for every pair of markers.  The code you cite, using pull.rf(), pulls out the two things as two separate square matrices, with rows and columns corresponding to markers.  But I'm not sure why you'd be interested in the column averages.

karl
